name: Malaysia
summary: No free movement for EU citizens. Every passport can use MM2H: Silver (USD 150,000 deposit and a RM600,000 home), Gold (USD 500,000 and RM1 million), Platinum (USD 1 million and RM2 million, with the right to do business) or the SEZ/SFZ tier (USD 32,000-65,000 in Johor zones). Very wealthy or high-earning people can use the PVIP (RM1 million deposit, RM200,000 fee, no minimum stay). Remote workers can use the DE Rantau Nomad Pass. None of these leads to permanent residence.
naturalisation: Citizenship by naturalisation (Federal Constitution Article 19) needs age 21+, about 10 of the last 12 years of residence, good character and Malay-language knowledge; it is discretionary and rare. The government portal says 12 years of residence.
dual_citizenship_note: Malaysia does not allow dual citizenship in principle; this run did not confirm the point from an official page.

routes.name: Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) - Silver
routes.summary: Five-year renewable social visit pass for foreigners who place USD 150,000 on fixed deposit and buy a home of RM600,000 or more.
routes.requirements: Fixed deposit in a Malaysian licensed bank; up to 50% may be withdrawn after approval for housing, education, medical care and tourism. Offshore income requirement dropped. Compulsory purchase of a residence after approval, which may not be sold for 10 years (upgrades allowed). Stay at least 90 days a year for participants aged 25 to 49. Medical check-up compulsory. Age 25+. Pass renewal fee RM1,500/RM3,000/RM5,000 per person for Silver/Gold/Platinum (per MOTAC fee table; period not stated). MM2H does not lead to permanent residence. Silver: fixed deposit USD 150,000; residence at least RM600,000; one-off participation fee RM1,000; pass valid 5 years with multiple-entry visa; business, investing or career not allowed.
routes.investment_options: USD 150,000 fixed deposit (recoverable, half withdrawable) plus purchase of a residence of at least RM600,000 (about USD 130,000).
routes.fees_note: One-off participation fee RM1,000; plus 8% SST per third-party summaries (not verified on official page).
routes.family: Spouse, children under 21 (and unmarried unemployed children 21-34), disabled children, parents and parents-in-law.
routes.tax_note: Pass does not make you tax resident (Malaysia: 182 days); foreign-sourced income received in Malaysia has special exemption rules not researched here.
routes.physical_presence: 90 days a year for participants aged 25 to 49; none stated for 50+

routes.summary: Twenty-year pass for a USD 1 million fixed deposit plus a home of RM2 million or more; the only tier allowing business and investment.
routes.requirements: Fixed deposit in a Malaysian licensed bank; up to 50% may be withdrawn after approval for housing, education, medical care and tourism. Offshore income requirement dropped. routes.name: Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) - SEZ/SFZ (Special Economic and Financial Zones)
routes.summary: Ten-year pass with the lowest deposit (USD 32,000 to 65,000) for buyers of property in Johor's special zones such as Forest City.
routes.requirements: Fixed deposit USD 65,000 for ages 21 to 49, USD 32,000 for age 50 and over; property purchase 'subject to the relevant state property purchase policy' (no federal minimum stated); participation fee RM1,000; pass valid 10 years; business or career not allowed. Minimum age 21. Other terms (90-day stay, 10-year hold) as the main MM2H tiers per MOTAC; confirm SEZ specifics with OSC MM2H.
routes.investment_options: USD 65,000 deposit for ages 21-49; USD 32,000 for 50+. Property in the zone per state policy.
routes.fees_note: Participation fee RM1,000; renewal fee RM300 per person.
routes.family: Spouse, children under 21 (and unmarried unemployed children 21-34), disabled children, parents and parents-in-law. (per main tiers; unverified for SEZ)
routes.physical_presence: Not separately stated; assumed same 90-day rule for under-50s (unverified)

routes.name: Malaysia Premium Visa Programme (PVIP)
routes.summary: Twenty-year visa for very high earners or wealthy people who deposit RM1 million and pay a RM200,000 participation fee, with no minimum stay and the right to work or run a business.
routes.requirements: Onshore plus offshore income of RM40,000 a month (RM480,000 a year) or total net worth of at least RM1 billion (as worded in the Immigration Department FAQ); fixed deposit of RM1,000,000 with a licensed Malaysian bank (50% withdrawable after 6 months for property, medical or education, with Immigration's letter); participation fee RM200,000 principal and RM100,000 per dependant (RM50,000 for the 10-year dependant option). Applications only via Immigration-authorised agencies. No age limit; no minimum-stay requirement; may work, study, buy real estate and run business.
routes.investment_options: RM1,000,000 fixed deposit (principal not withdrawable beyond 50% for stated purposes) plus RM200,000 participation fee.
routes.fees_note: Participation fee RM200,000 principal, RM100,000 per dependant; initial RM2,000 registration fee reported in a search snippet (unverified). Third-party sources report terms revised in March 2026; the FAQ read is undated.
routes.family: Spouse, children, parents and foreign domestic helpers may accompany.
routes.tax_note: Visa does not set tax residence.

routes.name: DE Rantau Nomad Pass (Professional Visit Pass)
routes.summary: One-year renewable pass for remote employees and freelancers working for clients abroad.
routes.requirements: Remote employee of a foreign company, or freelancer with client contracts of 3+ months; minimum annual income USD 24,000 (tech) or USD 60,000 (non-tech) per a 2026 secondary report, while an older MDEC FAQ gives USD 24,000 for all; age 18+; open to all nationalities except Israel; initial 12 months, renewable once for 12 more. Official FAQ version could not be opened, so income thresholds are unverified.
routes.fees_note: A third-party guide reports RM1,080 incl. 8% SST; not verified.
routes.family: Spouse and children may be added (not verified).
routes.tax_note: Tax residence follows the 182-day test; staying 182+ days makes you resident.

routes.name: Employment Pass (EP, Categories I-III)
routes.summary: Employer-sponsored work permit; the minimum salary was raised from 1 June 2026.
routes.requirements: Category I: basic salary at least RM20,000 a month (raised from RM10,000 effective 1 June 2026); Category II: RM10,000-19,999 (succession plan required); Category III: RM5,000-9,999 (RM7,000 for manufacturing). Figures are from law-firm summaries of the Expatriate Services Division decision; the official ESD notice was not opened. Dependant rights differ by category.
routes.family: Dependant passes for most categories (details unverified).
routes.physical_presence: Live and work in Malaysia for the sponsoring employer
